corrections.text: The article attributes the CVSS 8.8 score to "the National Vulnerability Database." The NVD page for CVE-2026-53359 states its own assessment is "not yet provided" (Base Score: N/A under the NIST/NVD row); the 8.8 figure shown on that page is a self-submitted score from the CNA (kernel.org), not an NVD analyst score. The number itself is accurate and independently corroborated by SUSE's own 8.8 (CVSS v3.1) rating, but the attribution to NVD as the scoring body is imprecise.

The article quotes CSO Online as describing ITScape as "a separate ARM64 KVM guest-to-host escape vulnerability disclosed by the same researcher in the previous month." This exact wording does not appear in the CSO Online article, which instead states Hyunwoo Kim "also disclosed a different KVM guest-to-host escape vulnerability dubbed ITScape (CVE-2026-46316) last month that works on ARM64 architecture." The underlying fact is accurate; the quotation marks misrepresent a paraphrase as verbatim text.

The article quotes the Cloud Security Alliance as stating CVE-2026-46113 "must be patched alongside CVE-2026-53359" for complete remediation. This exact phrase does not appear in the CSA research note, which conveys the same point in different words (an administrator who patches CVE-2026-53359 but misses the CVE-2026-46113 companion fix "remains exposed to the same underlying reuse flaw"). The underlying fact is accurate and independently corroborated elsewhere; the quotation marks misrepresent a paraphrase as verbatim text.
